raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds a ROCm (MI355X, gfx950) recipe and image for DeepSeek-V4-Flash GRPO where the vLLM rollout log-probs and the
trainer log-probs of the same tokens are **bitwise equal** (`rollout_probs_diff_max` = 0.0). It follows the pattern
of #7050 and #8146: a Dockerfile on `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.26.0` that applies patch files from
`docker/rocm/patches/`, plus a recipe.

- **Image** `docker/rocm/Dockerfile.rocm.deepseek-v4.true-on-policy`: the base (pinned by digest) and the TE / apex /
  libhsa / mbridge / Megatron-Bridge / transformers / TransferQueue pins of `Dockerfile.rocm.deepseek-v4`, then
  - the four existing DeepSeek-V4 vLLM patches, plus 18 vLLM batch-invariance patches (`vllm-bi-*.patch`);
  - Megatron-LM `ISEEKYAN/Megatron-LM` `ds4_vllm_align_preview` (the branch with mLite's vLLM-aligned DeepSeek-V4
    implementation, `impl=vllm`) plus 13 patches (`megatron-dsv4-*.patch`) that run it on ROCm;
  - a build-time `sha256sum -c` of every patched file, and closure checks (import paths, no start-up overlay).
- **Recipe** `examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_flash_true_on_policy_rocm.sh`: `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`
  (default) runs the consistent arm (batch-invariant rollout TP1 x DP8 x EP8 per node; mLite `impl=vllm` actor, CP4 x
  EP32, FSDP2); `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0` runs the Megatron-Core FP8-QAT baseline of
  `run_deepseek_v4_flash_megatron_rocm.sh`. Modelled on #7688.
- **verl fixes** the consistent arm needs:
  - `rollout.full_determinism` gave every request of a replica the same sampling seed, so the n samples of a GRPO
    group were identical and every advantage was 0. The seed is now derived from `(rollout.seed, request_id)`.
  - `enable_full_determinism` no longer fills every `torch.empty` with NaN
    (`torch.utils.deterministic.fill_uninitialized_memory = False`): tens of thousands of fill kernels per
    micro-batch, no effect on kernels that write their whole output.

Each patch header states what it fixes, why batch invariance needs it, and its upstream status. Several are already
on vLLM `main` after v0.26.0 (#49758, #59788, #59941) or covered by #52231; the DeepSeek-V4-specific ROCm kernels are
not yet proposed upstream, because vLLM `main` rewrote that attention path. Moving the rollout to vLLM `main` also
means porting the trainer's mirror of the forward, so this PR pins vLLM 0.26.0.

Related: #7688 (the NVIDIA preview of the same recipe), #8317 (GB200 image for Megatron Lite + batch-invariant
vLLM), #8146 / #7050 (the ROCm DeepSeek-V4 image this one extends).

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: `gh pr list --repo verl-project/verl --state all --search "true on-policy"`,
  `"batch invariant"`, `"deepseek-v4 rocm"`, `"full_determinism seed"`, `"per-request seed"`. Closest: #7688
  (NVIDIA, Megatron + vLLM main), #8317 (GB200 image), #7667 (router hash under `full_determinism`, a different
  file). None adds a ROCm true-on-policy image or the per-request seed fix.
- [x] Title format `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

CPU (this branch, torch 2.15.0+cpu):

```
pytest tests/workers/rollout/test_rollout_request_seed_on_cpu.py tests/workers/test_enable_full_determinism_on_cpu.py
6 passed
ruff 0.12.2 check + format --check on the changed Python files: clean
DRY_RUN=1 of the recipe for both arms and both profiles: rc 0
```

Source equivalence with the validated run (no GPU needed):
- vLLM: v0.26.0 + the 4 existing patches + the 18 new ones (`patch -p1 -F0`) is byte-identical to the vLLM tree
  of the validated run (2,629 files).
- Megatron-LM: 327a23823 + the 13 patches (`git apply`) is byte-identical to the validated tree in 48 of 49
  changed files; the 49th differs in one comment and one docstring line (AST identical).
- Recipe: the resolved command line equals the validated run's, except that `VLLM_BI_GEMM_TILES=1` is now set by
  the recipe instead of the container environment.

GPU, this image (built from this branch on MI355X; 4-layer DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base proxy, 1 node x 8, seed 42,
4 prompts x 8 samples, rollout TP1/DP8/EP8):

| arm | steps | result |
|---|---|---|
| consistent (BI=1), mLite impl=vllm CP4 x EP8, 14K responses | 3 | `rollout_probs_diff_max` 0.0 on every step |
| consistent (BI=1), same | 4 | 0.0 on every step, including step 4, whose rollout uses the weights synced after the first non-zero update (step 3) |
| native (BI=0), Megatron-Core PP1/CP1/EP8, PROFILE=proxy | 2 | trains end to end; probs_diff_max 0.24 / 0.37 (no batch invariance, as expected) |

The full-model run (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base, 4 nodes x 8, steps 1-3 against the validated run's metrics) is **still pending**.
The validated run used the same vLLM / Megatron sources and gave `rollout_probs_diff_max` 0.0 on all 36 steps, including after
an exact resume.

### API and Usage Example

```sh
DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build -f docker/rocm/Dockerfile.rocm.deepseek-v4.true-on-policy \
    -t verl-rocm:deepseek-v4-true-on-policy .
# in containers started with --ulimit nofile=1048576:1048576, on an existing 4-node Ray cluster:
MODEL_PATH=... TRAIN_FILES=... VAL_FILES=... \
    bash examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_flash_true_on_policy_rocm.sh
```

### Design & Code Changes

- `docker/rocm/patches/vllm-bi-*.patch` (18), `megatron-dsv4-*.patch` (13), `deepseek-v4-true-on-policy.sha256`.
- `docker/rocm/Dockerfile.rocm.deepseek-v4.true-on-policy`, `docker/rocm/README.md` (new section).
- `examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_flash_true_on_policy_rocm.sh`.
- `verl/workers/rollout/utils.py`, `verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/vllm_async_server.py`: per-request seed.
- `verl/workers/engine/utils.py`: no NaN fill under full determinism.
- `verl/workers/engine_workers.py`: skip trainer-side rollout weight quantization (with a warning) for engines that do not
  implement `set_rollout_weight_quantizer` (Megatron-LM mLite exports its own FP8 rollout weights).
- Tests: `tests/workers/rollout/test_rollout_request_seed_on_cpu.py`, `tests/workers/test_enable_full_determinism_on_cpu.py`.

### AI assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude). It is a draft: the author is reviewing every changed line and will
trim what is not needed before marking it ready. The author answers review comments personally.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] Apply pre-commit checks: pending
- [x] Add / Update the documentation: `docker/rocm/README.md`.
- [ ] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to the CI workflow: the two CPU tests run in the existing CPU unit-test job
  (`*_on_cpu.py`); the image and recipe need 4 x 8 MI355X, which CI does not have.
- [ ] The author reviewed every changed line.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,168 @@
+# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7
+# DeepSeek-V4-Flash true-on-policy RL on AMD MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3:
+# examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_flash_true_on_policy_rocm.sh
+#
+# Same base and pins as Dockerfile.rocm.deepseek-v4, plus
+#   - vLLM 0.26.0 batch-invariance patches for DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm (patches/vllm-bi-*.patch, applied after the
+#     four DeepSeek-V4 patches that Dockerfile.rocm.deepseek-v4 applies), and
+#   - Megatron-LM with mLite's vLLM-aligned DeepSeek-V4 implementation (impl=vllm) on ROCm: ISEEKYAN/Megatron-LM
+#     ds4_vllm_align_preview plus patches/megatron-dsv4-*.patch.
+# With VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 the rollout log-probs and the trainer log-probs of the same tokens are bitwise equal.
+# Every patched file is checked against patches/deepseek-v4-true-on-policy.sha256 at build time.
+#
+# Build from the repository root:
+#   DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build -f docker/rocm/Dockerfile.rocm.deepseek-v4.true-on-policy \
+#     -t verl-rocm:deepseek-v4-true-on-policy .
+
+ARG BASE_IMAGE=vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.26.0
+# What the v0.26.0 tag resolved to on 2026-10-19.
+ARG BASE_IMAGE_DIGEST=sha256:5709fafe47123becb2f5e61c32d0b97beff1a629bb40bb753c15464f69a97a18
+FROM ${BASE_IMAGE}@${BASE_IMAGE_DIGEST}
+
+# Keep the base image's ROCm torch/Triton: later pip steps must not replace them (TransferQueue -> tensordict 0.15
+# -> torch>=2.13 otherwise pulls a CUDA torch over the ROCm one).
+RUN python3 -c "import importlib.metadata as m; [print(f'{p}=={m.version(p)}') for p in ('torch','triton','torchvision','torchaudio') if any(d.metadata['Name'].lower()==p for d in m.distributions())]" > /opt/base-constraints.txt && cat /opt/base-constraints.txt
+ENV PIP_CONSTRAINT=/opt/base-constraints.txt
+
+# --- Binary dependencies, verified by sha256 ---------------------------------------------------------------------
+ARG APEX_WHEEL_URL="https://repo.radeon.com/rocm/manylinux/rocm-rel-7.2.3/apex-1.9.0%2Brocm7.2.3.git355db9b8-cp312-cp312-linux_x86_64.whl"
+ARG APEX_WHEEL_SHA256=d1341f79447a30fa4ac951511ade506d3c4afc66c6f8c9f4660126a20dd62109
+# Transformer Engine (ROCm) 2.18.0.dev0+8c116a51b: Triton grouped GEMM (avoids the BF16 grouped-GEMM backward hang
+# on gfx950) and the float-scale blockwise FP8 GEMM.
+ARG TE_WHEEL=transformer_engine-2.18.0.dev0+8c116a51b-cp312-cp312-linux_x86_64.whl
+ARG TE_WHEEL_URL="https://github.com/PeterYang12/Daily_LLM/releases/download/v0.0.2/${TE_WHEEL}"
+ARG TE_WHEEL_SHA256=214b5e3e5c304e3ab193770def965cf88d5faafd1d5c882f82390b7e311b66f5
+# ROCm 7.2.x does not return memory for large allocations with expandable_segments; this libhsa build fixes that.
+ARG LIBHSA_URL="https://github.com/PeterYang12/Daily_LLM/releases/download/v0.0.1/libhsa-runtime64.so.1.18.0"
+ARG LIBHSA_SHA256=07e53330baa28ef4d50a8ec5d34edbcc2c2f1b889fc80d3d3fc564f499273e4f
+RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip <<'EOF'
+set -eux
+mkdir -p /tmp/dl
+wget -q -O "/tmp/dl/apex-1.9.0+rocm7.2.3.git355db9b8-cp312-cp312-linux_x86_64.whl" "${APEX_WHEEL_URL}"
+wget -q -O "/tmp/dl/${TE_WHEEL}" "${TE_WHEEL_URL}"
+wget -q -O /tmp/dl/libhsa-runtime64.so.1.18.0 "${LIBHSA_URL}"
+printf '%s  %s\n' \
+  "${APEX_WHEEL_SHA256}" "/tmp/dl/apex-1.9.0+rocm7.2.3.git355db9b8-cp312-cp312-linux_x86_64.whl" \
+  "${TE_WHEEL_SHA256}" "/tmp/dl/${TE_WHEEL}" \
+  "${LIBHSA_SHA256}" /tmp/dl/libhsa-runtime64.so.1.18.0 | sha256sum -c -
+pip install /tmp/dl/apex-*.whl
+pip install --no-build-isolation "/tmp/dl/${TE_WHEEL}"
+install -m 0644 /tmp/dl/libhsa-runtime64.so.1.18.0 /opt/rocm-7.2.3/lib/libhsa-runtime64.so.1.18.70203
+rm -rf /tmp/dl
+EOF
+
+# --- Python dependencies ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ARG MBRIDGE_COMMIT=0cd4ae23f2425da77a80cb3f517828452fa8e984
+# Megatron-Bridge with the UE8M0 export fix (FP8 weight export keeps the power-of-two scale grid).
+ARG MEGATRON_BRIDGE_COMMIT=658c695c560b5cfcb6ccfedc35bf9d3f6f747ffe
+RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip <<'EOF'
+set -eux
+pip install "git+https://github.com/ISEEKYAN/mbridge.git@${MBRIDGE_COMMIT}" mathruler==0.1.0 qwen-vl-utils==0.0.14 \
+  flash-linear-attention==0.5.2
+pip install --no-deps nvidia-modelopt==0.47.0 PuLP==3.3.2
+pip install --no-deps --no-build-isolation --ignore-requires-python \
+  "git+https://github.com/PeterYang12/Megatron-Bridge@${MEGATRON_BRIDGE_COMMIT}"
+pip install transformers==5.12.1 TransferQueue==0.1.11 tensordict==0.10.0
+# verl's install_requires that are not in the base image (verl itself is installed --no-deps below).

+## DeepSeek-V4-Flash true on-policy (MI355X)
+
+[`Dockerfile.rocm.deepseek-v4.true-on-policy`](Dockerfile.rocm.deepseek-v4.true-on-policy) builds the image for
+[`examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_flash_true_on_policy_rocm.sh`](../../examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_flash_true_on_policy_rocm.sh):
+GRPO on DeepSeek-V4-Flash (FP8) where the vLLM rollout log-probs and the trainer log-probs of the same tokens are
+bitwise equal (`rollout_probs_diff_max` = 0).
+
+- Base `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.26.0`, pinned by digest; Transformer Engine, apex, libhsa, Megatron-Bridge and
+  mbridge as in `Dockerfile.rocm.deepseek-v4`.
+- vLLM: the four DeepSeek-V4 patches of `Dockerfile.rocm.deepseek-v4`, then `patches/vllm-bi-*.patch`
+  (batch-invariant kernels and collectives for DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm). Each patch header states what it fixes and
+  its upstream status.
+- Megatron-LM: `ISEEKYAN/Megatron-LM` `ds4_vllm_align_preview` plus `patches/megatron-dsv4-*.patch` (mLite's
+  vLLM-aligned DeepSeek-V4 implementation, `impl=vllm`, on ROCm).
+- The build checks every patched file against `patches/deepseek-v4-true-on-policy.sha256`.
+
+```sh
+DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build \
+    -f docker/rocm/Dockerfile.rocm.deepseek-v4.true-on-policy \
+    -t verl-rocm:deepseek-v4-true-on-policy .
+```
+
+The recipe selects the arm with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` (1: batch-invariant rollout + mLite `impl=vllm` actor;
+0: default vLLM kernels + Megatron-Core actor with FP8 QAT). The full profile is 4 nodes x 8 GPUs: actor
+CP4 x EP32 with FSDP2, rollout TP1 x DP8 x EP8 per node. Multi-node runs need an existing Ray cluster whose
+workers run this image, and containers started with `--ulimit nofile=1048576:1048576` (the default open-file
+limit ran out in gloo after ~26 steps).

++"""Block-scaled FP8 fake quantization for BF16 training (quantization-aware training).
++
++The GEMMs of the model keep running in BF16, but their operands are rounded through
++FP8 (E4M3) the way a block-scaled FP8 inference engine rounds them, so the policy
++the optimizer sees is the policy the inference engine serves. Every rounding is
++wrapped in a straight-through estimator: the forward uses the rounded value, the
++backward passes the gradient to the unrounded tensor unchanged.
++
++The recipe is the one DeepSeek checkpoints are stored and served in:
++
++* weights: one scale per 128x128 tile, powers of two (``scale_fmt: ue8m0``);
++* activations: one scale per 128 values along the reduction axis, recomputed on
++  every forward, plain float32 (power-of-two optional, for DeepGEMM-style kernels);
++* KV cache (DeepSeek-V4): E4M3 with one power-of-two scale per 64 NoPE channels
++  of the KV latent, RoPE channels kept in BF16;
++* indexer (DeepSeek-V4): queries and keys in E4M3 with one power-of-two scale per
++  vector.
++
++Everything is driven by ``TransformerConfig`` (``fp8_fake_quant``,
++``fp8_fake_quant_kv_cache``, ``fp8_fake_quant_indexer_qk`` and their block sizes).
++The linear-layer part hooks the Transformer Engine wrappers in
++``megatron.core.extensions.transformer_engine``; the attention-side parts are called
++from the DeepSeek-V4 attention and CSA modules.
++
++Combined with FP8 training (``fp8`` set) the TE linear layers are left to Transformer
++Engine and ``fp8_fake_quant`` only rounds the DeepSeek-V4 grouped output projection, so
++the same switches give the rollout-matching forward in both training modes.
++"""

++from typing import List

++import torch
++import torch.nn.functional as F
++
++from megatron.core.model_parallel_config import ModelParallelConfig
++
++E4M3_MAX = 448.0
++
++_EXCLUDED_ATTR = "_fp8_fake_quant_excluded"
++
++
++def _scale_from_amax(
++    amax: torch.Tensor, pow2_scale: bool, amax_floor: float | None = None
++) -> torch.Tensor:
++    """Per-block scale from the block's absolute maximum.
++
++    ``amax_floor`` reproduces kernels that clamp the amax before taking the
++    exponent; the remaining ``tiny`` clamp only keeps an all-zero block (which
++    rounds to zero regardless) away from a division by zero.
++    """
++    if amax_floor is not None:
++        amax = amax.clamp(min=amax_floor)
++    scale = (amax / E4M3_MAX).clamp(min=torch.finfo(torch.float32).tiny)
++    if pow2_scale:
++        scale = torch.exp2(torch.ceil(torch.log2(scale)))
++    return scale
++
++
++def _round_to_e4m3(values: torch.Tensor, scale: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
++    """Quantize ``values`` (float32) to E4M3 with ``scale`` and dequantize again."""
++    return (values / scale).clamp(-E4M3_MAX, E4M3_MAX).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).float() * scale
++
++
++def _straight_through(x: torch.Tensor, rounded: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
++    """Forward ``rounded``, backward the identity on ``x``."""
++    return x + (rounded.to(x.dtype) - x).detach()
++
++
++def fake_quant_weight_blockwise(
++    weight: torch.Tensor, block_size: int = 128, pow2_scale: bool = True
++) -> torch.Tensor:
++    """Round a 2D weight through E4M3 with one scale per ``block_size`` square tile.
++
++    Tiles start at the top-left corner, as in the checkpoint layout; a dimension
++    that is not a multiple of ``block_size`` gets a partial tile at its end.
++    """
++    if weight.dim() != 2:
++        raise ValueError(f"fake_quant_weight_blockwise expects a 2D weight, got {weight.shape}")
++    rows, cols = weight.shape
++    pad_r, pad_c = (-rows) % block_size, (-cols) % block_size
++
++    values = weight.detach().float()
++    if pad_r or pad_c:
++        values = F.pad(values, (0, pad_c, 0, pad_r))
++    tiled = values.reshape(
++        values.shape[0] // block_size, block_size, values.shape[1] // block_size, block_size

++    if pad_r or pad_c:
++        rounded = rounded[:rows, :cols]
++    return _straight_through(weight, rounded)
++
++
++def fake_quant_activation_groupwise(

++    """Round an activation through E4M3 with one scale per ``group_size`` values of its last dim."""

++    pad = (-last) % group_size

++    values = x.detach().float()
++    if pad:
++        values = F.pad(values, (0, pad))
++    grouped = values.reshape(*values.shape[:-1], values.shape[-1] // group_size, group_size)
++    scale = _scale_from_amax(grouped.abs().amax(dim=-1, keepdim=True), pow2_scale)
++    rounded = _round_to_e4m3(grouped, scale).reshape(values.shape)
++    if pad:
++        rounded = rounded[..., :last]
++    return _straight_through(x, rounded)
++

++def fake_quant_kv_latent(kv: torch.Tensor, rope_dim: int, block_size: int = 64) -> torch.Tensor:
++    """Round a KV latent ``[..., head_dim]`` the way an FP8 KV cache stores it.
++
++    The leading ``head_dim - rope_dim`` (NoPE) channels become E4M3 with one
++    power-of-two scale per ``block_size`` channels; the trailing ``rope_dim``
++    channels are returned untouched. The amax is floored at 1e-4 before the
++    exponent is taken, as the cache-write kernel does.
++    """
++    nope = kv.shape[-1] - rope_dim
++    if nope <= 0 or nope % block_size:
++        raise ValueError(
++            f"fake_quant_kv_latent: {kv.shape[-1]} channels minus {rope_dim} RoPE channels is not "
++            f"a multiple of the KV block size {block_size}"

++    head, tail = kv[..., :nope], kv[..., nope:]

++    grouped = head.detach().float().reshape(*head.shape[:-1], nope // block_size, block_size)
++    scale = _scale_from_amax(
++        grouped.abs().amax(dim=-1, keepdim=True), pow2_scale=True, amax_floor=1e-4
++    )
++    rounded = _round_to_e4m3(grouped, scale).reshape(head.shape)
++    return torch.cat((_straight_through(head, rounded), tail), dim=-1)
++
++
++def fake_quant_per_vector(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
++    """Round ``x`` through E4M3 with one power-of-two scale over its whole last dim."""
++    values = x.detach().float()
++    scale = _scale_from_amax(
++        values.abs().amax(dim=-1, keepdim=True), pow2_scale=True, amax_floor=1e-10
++    )
++    return _straight_through(x, _round_to_e4m3(values, scale))
++
++
++def exclude_from_fp8_fake_quant(module: torch.nn.Module) -> torch.nn.Module:
++    """Keep a linear module out of ``fp8_fake_quant``.

++    For the projections an FP8 checkpoint stores in BF16 and the inference engine

++    """
++    setattr(module, _EXCLUDED_ATTR, True)

++
++
++def fp8_fake_quant_active(module: torch.nn.Module) -> bool:

++    Under FP8 training (``config.fp8`` set) the TE linear layers already compute in FP8,

++    """Per sequence: start row, first visible compressed group, visible token count, token prefix sum.

++    first_group = ((range_start - int(d_comp) - seq_start).clamp_min(0) + int(ratio) - 1) // int(
++        ratio

++    count = torch.where(active, (stop_group - first_group).clamp_min(0), torch.zeros_like(stop_group))

++            if cu[s] <= gq < cu[s + 1]:
++                ssf = cu[s]

++                    scs = cu_c[s]; scl = cu_c[s + 1] - scs

++                    ws = max(gq - W + 1, ssf); wc = gq - ws + 1
++                    if mode == 2:
++                        if col < cw:
++                            cid = topk[row][col]

++def k_compact_src(cu, gs, l_local, ratio, d_comp, compact_len):

++    # vLLM's mhc_pre_torch (FP32 there, FP64 here) + the RMSNorm of the layer input.

++    mixes = F.linear(flat, fn) * torch.rsqrt(flat.square().mean(-1, keepdim=True) + rms_eps)
++    pre_mix, post_mix, comb_mix = mixes.split([mult, mult, mult * mult], dim=-1)
++    base_pre, base_post, base_comb = base.split([mult, mult, mult * mult], dim=-1)
++    pre = torch.sigmoid(pre_mix * scale[0] + base_pre) + eps
++    post = 2 * torch.sigmoid(post_mix * scale[1] + base_post)

++    comb = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1) + eps

++"""DeepSeek-V4 trainer forward = the rollout's vLLM forward; backward = the Lite model's native recompute.
++
++Sub-module granularity (``primitive.ops.visible_vjp``): each unit's value comes from the in-process vLLM engine's
++own module (bitwise what the rollout serves; the engine supplies attention metadata, KV cache and batch geometry),
++and its VJP from the Lite module of the same math recomputed at the unit's visible inputs on the trainer's masters:
++
++  unit                 visible (vLLM)                 native (Lite masters)
++  embedding            embed_input_ids                F.embedding
++  mHC pre / post       mhc_pre / mhc_post ops         hca.mhc_pre / hca.mhc_post (vLLM's torch semantics, FP32)
++  attn / ffn norm      RMSNorm                        Lite RMSNorm
++  attention            DeepSeek-V4 attention          Lite CSA, compressed top-k pinned to the vLLM indexer's
++  MoE                  FusedMoE                       Lite MoE, expert ids pinned (RouterReplay REPLAY_FORWARD)
++  HC head              hc_head op                     hca.mhc_head
++  final norm           RMSNorm                        Lite RMSNorm
++  LM head              compute_logits                 F.linear
++
++Quantized weights enter the native graph at the value the rollout serves (``deployed_values``): dX uses that
++value, dW reaches the BF16 master (identity STE). While the checkpoint's source scales are still bound (before the
++first update) the masters already are that value.
++
++FSDP2 masters (``optimizer=fsdp2``): the forward runs as the forward of the Lite module that owns each part's
++parameters -- the root for the whole model, each decoder layer for its units, a nested FSDP2 module (the routed
++experts) for the unit that contains it -- so FSDP2's own hooks bracket it as they bracket a native forward: unshard
++before (all-gather), reshard after, unshard again when the backward reaches its output, and reshard plus
++reduce-scatter the gradients once the backward is through its input. The native recompute (at backward) therefore
++finds its masters unsharded, and the nested experts in the pre-backward state FSDP2 keeps for activation
++checkpointing (their recompute forward neither unshards nor reshards).
++"""

++from __future__ import annotations

++from collections.abc import Callable
++from typing import Any

++import torch
++import torch.nn.functional as F
++from torch.distributed.fsdp import FSDPModule

++from megatron.lite.model.deepseek_v4.lite.model import DeepseekV4Layer, DeepseekV4MTPLayer
++from megatron.lite.primitive.modules import router_replay

++# 2-D parameters the rollout serves as block FP8.  Everything 2-D under attention / experts /
++# shared experts, except what the rollout keeps in BF16: the compressor, the indexer's
++# weights_proj, the router gate, norms and mHC.
++_QUANTIZED_KEYS = (
++    "wq_a", "wkv", "wq_b", "wo_a", "wo_b", "fc1", "fc2", "gate_up", "down", "linear_fc1", "linear_fc2",
++)

++def training_visible_model_class(base: type) -> type:
++    """vLLM's DeepSeek-V4 model class whose step forward a bound training forward can take over.
++
++    Registered under the same architecture name for the trainer's private engine only
++    (``primitive.vllm_engine.register_model_class``). With nothing bound it is the base class."""
++
++    class TrainingVisibleDeepseekV4ForCausalLM(base):
++        def __init__(self, *, vllm_config, prefix: str = ""):
++            super().__init__(vllm_config=vllm_config, prefix=prefix)
++            self._training_forward: Callable | None = None
++
++        def bind_training_forward(self, fn: Callable | None) -> None:
++            self._training_forward = fn
++
++        def forward(self, input_ids, positions, intermediate_tensors=None, inputs_embeds=None, **kwargs):
++            fn = self._training_forward
++            if fn is not None:
++                hidden = fn(input_ids, positions)
++                if hidden is not None:
++                    return hidden
++            return super().forward(input_ids, positions, intermediate_tensors, inputs_embeds, **kwargs)
++
++    TrainingVisibleDeepseekV4ForCausalLM.__qualname__ = TrainingVisibleDeepseekV4ForCausalLM.__name__
++    return TrainingVisibleDeepseekV4ForCausalLM
++
++
++def _as_forward(module: torch.nn.Module, fn: Callable, *args):
++    """``fn(*args)``; if ``module`` is FSDP2-sharded, run as ``module``'s forward so its FSDP2 hooks bracket it."""
++    if not isinstance(module, FSDPModule):
++        return fn(*args)
++    own = module.__dict__.get("forward")  # an instance-level wrapper, e.g. activation checkpointing
++    module.forward = fn
++    try:
++        return module(*args)
++    finally:
++        if own is None:
++            del module.forward
++        else:
++            module.forward = own
++
++
++def _fsdp_within(module: torch.nn.Module) -> list[torch.nn.Module]:
++    """FSDP2 modules nested in ``module`` (``module`` included), outermost first."""
++    return [m for m in module.modules() if isinstance(m, FSDPModule)]
++
++
++def _packed_seq_params(positions: torch.Tensor):
++    from megatron.core.packed_seq_params import PackedSeqParams
++
++    starts = (positions == 0).nonzero().flatten().to(torch.int32)
++    total = torch.tensor([positions.numel()], dtype=torch.int32, device=positions.device)
++    cu_seqlens = torch.cat([starts, total])
++    max_len = int((cu_seqlens[1:] - cu_seqlens[:-1]).max())
++    return PackedSeqParams(
++        qkv_format="thd",
++        cu_seqlens_q=cu_seqlens,
++        cu_seqlens_kv=cu_seqlens,
++        max_seqlen_q=max_len,
++        max_seqlen_kv=max_len,
++    )
++
++
++class VisibleDeepseekV4:
++    """Binds the engine's vLLM ``DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`` (visible) to a Lite ``DeepseekV4Model`` (masters)."""
++
++    def __init__(
++        self,
++        vllm_model,
++        lite_model: torch.nn.Module,
++        model_cfg,
++        *,
++        deployed_value: Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor],
++        max_tokens: int,
++    ):
++        self.v = vllm_model
++        self.lite = lite_model
++        self.cfg = model_cfg
++        self.deployed_value = deployed_value
++        # By class, not name: FSDP2 (``fully_shard``) swaps a unit's class for an ``FSDP<name>`` subclass.
++        self.lite_layers = [
++            m for m in lite_model.modules()
++            if isinstance(m, DeepseekV4Layer) and not isinstance(m, DeepseekV4MTPLayer)
++        ]
++        inner = vllm_model.model
++        self.layer_ids = list(range(inner.start_layer, inner.end_layer))
++        if len(self.layer_ids) != len(self.lite_layers):
++            raise RuntimeError(
++                f"vLLM serves {len(self.layer_ids)} decoder layers, the Lite chunk has {len(self.lite_layers)}"
++            )
++        if not hasattr(lite_model, "_fp8_source_scales_valid"):
++            raise RuntimeError("Lite model has no bound FP8 source-scale state (load_hf_weights not run?)")
++
++        # Discrete state of the visible forward, consumed by the native recompute.
++        self._pins: dict[int, dict[str, torch.Tensor]] = {}
++        self._capturing = False
++        self._num_tokens = 0
++        self._routing = RoutingCapture(
++            {
++                layer: inner.layers[layer].ffn.experts.router
++                for layer in self.layer_ids
++            },
++            max_tokens=max_tokens,
++            top_k=model_cfg.num_experts_per_tok,
++            device=torch.device("cuda", torch.cuda.current_device()),
++        )
++        for layer in self.layer_ids:
++            indexer = getattr(inner.layers[layer].attn, "indexer", None)
++            if indexer is not None:
++                indexer.register_forward_hook(self._indexer_hook(layer))
++
++        # Lite RouterReplay: one instance per MoE router, mapped to its decoder layer.
++        self._n_replay = router_replay.attach_router_replay(lite_model)
++        instances = router_replay.RouterReplay.global_router_replay_instances
++        if len(instances) != self._n_replay:
++            raise RuntimeError("router-replay instance registry does not match this model")
++        position = {id(instance): i for i, instance in enumerate(instances)}
++        self._replay_index: dict[int, int] = {}
++        for index, layer in enumerate(self.lite_layers):
++            owned = [
++                position[id(m.router_replay)]
++                for m in layer.modules()
++                if getattr(m, "router_replay", None) is not None and id(m.router_replay) in position
++            ]
++            if len(owned) > 1:
++                raise RuntimeError(f"decoder layer {index} owns {len(owned)} router-replay instances")
++            if owned:
++                self._replay_index[index] = owned[0]
++
++        self._quantized = {i: self._quantized_names(layer) for i, layer in enumerate(self.lite_layers)}
++        # FSDP2 modules nested in a layer's attention / MoE (lite wiring: the routed experts, on the expert-DP mesh).
++        self._fsdp_attn = {i: _fsdp_within(layer.self_attn) for i, layer in enumerate(self.lite_layers)}
++        self._fsdp_moe = {i: _fsdp_within(layer.mlp) for i, layer in enumerate(self.lite_layers)}
++
++    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ discrete-state capture
++    def _indexer_hook(self, layer: int):
++        def hook(module, args, output):
++            if self._capturing:
++                self._pins.setdefault(layer, {})["indexer_topk"] = output[: self._num_tokens].detach().clone()
++
++        return hook
++
++    @staticmethod
++    def _quantized_names(lite_layer) -> list[str]:
++        """``.name`` within the layer of every master the rollout serves as block FP8."""
++        return [
++            "." + n
++            for n, p in lite_layer.named_parameters()
++            if p.dim() == 2
++            and any(k in n for k in _QUANTIZED_KEYS)
++            and not any(k in n for k in _UNQUANTIZED_KEYS)
++        ]
++
++    def _served(self, index: int, scope: str):
++        """Context: the layer's quantized masters under ``scope`` take their served value.
++
++        Looked up by name at use: under FSDP2 the module holds a different (unsharded) parameter while unsharded."""
++        layer = self.lite_layers[index]
++        params = [layer.get_parameter(n[1:]) for n in self._quantized[index] if scope in n]
++        return deployed_values(
++            params, self.deployed_value, active=not bool(self.lite._fp8_source_scales_valid)
++        )
++
++    def unit(self, visible: Callable, native: Callable, *inputs):
++        """One visible/native unit (overridable, e.g. to record units in tests)."""
++        return visible_forward(visible, native, *inputs)
++
++    def _owned_unit(self, owners: list[torch.nn.Module], visible: Callable, native: Callable, x):
++        """A unit run as the forward of the FSDP2 modules (outermost first) whose masters its native uses."""
++        if not owners:
++            return self.unit(visible, native, x)
++        return _as_forward(owners[0], lambda t: self._owned_unit(owners[1:], visible, native, t), x)
++
++    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ one decoder layer
++    def _layer(self, index: int, x, positions, input_ids, psp, pins):
++        layer_id = self.layer_ids[index]
++        vl, ll, cfg = self.v.model.layers[layer_id], self.lite_layers[index], self.cfg
++        tokens = x.shape[0]
++        position_ids = positions.view(1, tokens)
++
++        def hc_pre(residual, fn, scale, base, hc):
++            def visible(r):
++                return vl.mhc_pre(
++                    residual=r, fn=fn, hc_scale=scale, hc_base=base, rms_eps=vl.rms_norm_eps,
++                    hc_pre_eps=vl.hc_eps, hc_sinkhorn_eps=vl.hc_eps,
++                    hc_post_mult_value=vl.hc_post_alpha, sinkhorn_repeat=vl.hc_sinkhorn_iters,
++                )
++
++            def native(r):
++                return mhc_pre(
++                    r, hc.fn.float(), hc.scale.float(), hc.base.float(), vl.rms_norm_eps,
++                    vl.hc_eps, vl.hc_eps, vl.hc_post_alpha, vl.hc_sinkhorn_iters,
++                )
++
++            return self.unit(visible, native, residual)
++
++        def hc_post(out, residual, post, comb):
++            return self.unit(lambda *a: vl.mhc_post(*a), mhc_post, out, residual, post, comb)
++
++        # attention block
++        residual = x
++        post, comb, h = hc_pre(x, vl.hc_attn_fn, vl.hc_attn_scale, vl.hc_attn_base, ll.attn_hc)
++        h = self.unit(
++            lambda t: vl.attn_norm(t),
++            lambda t: ll.input_layernorm(t.view(tokens, 1, -1)).view(tokens, -1),
++            h,
++        )
++
++        def attention_native(t):
++            with self._served(index, ".self_attn."):
++                return ll.self_attn(
++                    t.view(tokens, 1, -1),
++                    position_ids=position_ids,
++                    packed_seq_params=psp,
++                    pinned_indexer_topk=pins.get(layer_id, {}).get("indexer_topk"),
++                ).view(tokens, -1)
++
++        h = self._owned_unit(self._fsdp_attn[index], lambda t: vl.attn(positions, t, None), attention_native, h)
++        x = hc_post(h, residual, post, comb)
++
++        # MoE block
++        residual = x
++        post, comb, h = hc_pre(x, vl.hc_ffn_fn, vl.hc_ffn_scale, vl.hc_ffn_base, ll.ffn_hc)
++        h = self.unit(
++            lambda t: vl.ffn_norm(t),
++            lambda t: ll.post_attention_layernorm(t.view(tokens, 1, -1)).view(tokens, -1),
++            h,
++        )
++
++        def moe_native(t):
++            if index not in self._replay_index:
++                raise RuntimeError(f"no router-replay instance for decoder layer {index}")
++            expert_ids = pins[layer_id]["expert_ids"]
++            replay = [
++                torch.zeros(tokens, cfg.num_experts_per_tok, dtype=torch.int64, device=t.device)
++                for _ in range(self._n_replay)
++            ]
++            replay[self._replay_index[index]] = expert_ids
++            router_replay.RouterReplay.set_replay_data(replay)
++            router_replay.RouterReplay.set_global_router_replay_action(
++                router_replay.RouterReplayAction.REPLAY_FORWARD
++            )
++            try:
++                with self._served(index, ".mlp."):
++                    return ll.mlp(t.view(tokens, 1, -1), input_ids=input_ids.view(1, tokens)).view(tokens, -1)
++            finally:
++                router_replay.RouterReplay.clear_global_state()
++
++        h = self._owned_unit(self._fsdp_moe[index], lambda t: vl.ffn(t, input_ids), moe_native, h)
++        if self._capturing:
++            pins.setdefault(layer_id, {})["expert_ids"] = self._routing.take(layer_id, tokens)
++        return hc_post(h, residual, post, comb)
++
++    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ whole model
++    def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor, positions: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
++        """Final hidden states ``[T, hidden]`` of one packed prefill, with the autograd graph described above.
++
++        Must run inside the engine's model forward (it uses the engine's forward context)."""
++        tokens = input_ids.shape[0]
++        # A fresh dict per forward: this forward's native closures keep it until their backward.
++        pins = self._pins = {}
++        self._num_tokens = tokens
++        self._capturing = True
++        self._routing.reset()
++        try:
++            # The root owns the embedding, the final norm and the LM head (and runs FSDP2's per-forward setup).
++            return _as_forward(self.lite, lambda ids, pos: self._model(ids, pos, pins), input_ids, positions)
++        finally:
++            self._capturing = False
++
++    def _model(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor, positions: torch.Tensor, pins) -> torch.Tensor:
++        inner = self.v.model
++        tokens = input_ids.shape[0]
++        psp = _packed_seq_params(positions)
++        h = self.unit(
++            lambda ids: inner.embed_input_ids(ids),
++            lambda ids: F.embedding(ids, self._lite_param("embed_tokens", self.cfg.vocab_size)),
++            input_ids,
++        )
++        h = h.unsqueeze(-2).repeat(1, inner.hc_mult, 1)
++        for index in range(len(self.layer_ids)):
++            h = _as_forward(
++                self.lite_layers[index],
++                lambda t, index=index: self._layer(index, t, positions, input_ids, psp, pins),
++                h,
++            )
++        head = self._lite_module("hc_head")
++        h = self.unit(
++            lambda t: inner.hc_head_op(
++                t, inner.hc_head_fn, inner.hc_head_scale, inner.hc_head_base,
++                inner.rms_norm_eps, inner.hc_eps,
++            ),
++            lambda t: mhc_head(
++                t, head.hc_fn.float(), head.hc_scale.float(), head.hc_base.float(),
++                inner.rms_norm_eps, inner.hc_eps,
++            ),
++            h,
++        )
++        norm = self._lite_module("norm")
++        return self.unit(
++            lambda t: inner.norm(t),
++            lambda t: norm(t.view(tokens, 1, -1)).view(tokens, -1),
++            h,
++        )
++
++    def logits(self, hidden: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
++        return self.unit(
++            lambda t: self.v.compute_logits(t),
++            lambda t: F.linear(t, self._lite_param("lm_head", self.cfg.vocab_size)).float(),
++            hidden,
++        )
++
++    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ Lite lookups
++    def _lite_param(self, prefix: str, rows: int) -> torch.nn.Parameter:
++        for name, param in self.lite.named_parameters():
++            if name.startswith(prefix) and name.endswith("weight") and param.shape[0] == rows:
++                return param
++        raise RuntimeError(f"Lite parameter under {prefix!r} not found")
++
++    def _lite_module(self, name: str) -> torch.nn.Module:
++        module = getattr(self.lite, name, None)
++        if module is None:
++            raise RuntimeError(f"Lite model has no {name!r} (not the last pipeline stage?)")
++        return module
++

++def selected_log_probs(
++    logits: torch.Tensor,
++    labels: torch.Tensor,
++    *,
++    temperature: float | torch.Tensor = 1.0,
++    vocab_limit: int | None = None,
++    calculate_entropy: bool = False,
++) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
++    """Log-probabilities of ``labels`` as the rollout's sampler computes them: logits beyond ``vocab_limit``
++    masked to -inf (an integration that masks them at rollout), FP32, divided by the temperature, log-softmax."""
++    if vocab_limit is not None and vocab_limit < logits.shape[-1]:
++        logits = logits.clone()
++        logits[..., vocab_limit:] = float("-inf")
++    logits = logits.float()
++    if isinstance(temperature, torch.Tensor) or float(temperature) != 1.0:
++        logits = logits / temperature
++    log_softmax = torch.log_softmax(logits, dim=-1)
++    out = {"log_probs": log_softmax.gather(1, labels.reshape(-1, 1).long()).squeeze(1)}
++    if calculate_entropy:
++        probs = log_softmax.exp()
++        out["entropy"] = -(probs * log_softmax.masked_fill(probs == 0, 0)).sum(-1)
++    return out

++inference consistency: the rollout's own kernel, bitwise equal to what the rollout served) run without building an
++autograd graph -- and differentiates ``native(*inputs)`` instead: the training implementation of the same math,
++recomputed from the saved inputs at backward time with autograd. Backward precision and speed are ``native``'s; the
++forward value is ``visible``'s. Integer inputs (token ids, pinned discrete selections) pass through without gradient.
++
++Quantized weights: ``deployed_values(params, value_fn)`` gives each master parameter the value the rollout serves
++(``value_fn(master)``, e.g. dequant(requant(master))) for the duration of the native recompute *and its backward*, so
++dX uses the served value while dW lands on the master (identity STE). Restoring the masters is deferred until the
++recompute's backward has run because some modules (TE GroupedLinear) re-read their weight parameters in backward.

++from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Iterator

++
++    :class:`VisibleNativeFunction` calls this after each native recompute's backward; callers that run a native
++    function and its backward themselves must call it afterwards."""
++    while _DEFERRED:
++        _DEFERRED.pop()()

++    anchor = _ANCHORS.get(device)
++    if anchor is None:
++        anchor = _ANCHORS[device] = torch.zeros((), device=device, requires_grad=True)
++    return anchor

++            *[x.detach() if torch.is_tensor(x) else torch.empty(0) for x in inputs]
++        )
++        ctx.non_tensors = [(False, None) if torch.is_tensor(x) else (True, x) for x in inputs]
++        return outputs if is_tuple else outputs[0]
++
++    @staticmethod
++    def backward(ctx, *grad_outputs):
++        inputs = []
++        for saved, is_float, (is_other, other) in zip(
++            ctx.saved_tensors, ctx.float_inputs, ctx.non_tensors
++        ):
++            if is_other:
++                inputs.append(other)
++            else:
++                inputs.append(saved.detach().requires_grad_(True) if is_float else saved)
++        try:
++            with torch.enable_grad():
++                output = ctx.native(*inputs)
++                outputs = output if isinstance(output, tuple) else (output,)
++                pairs = [
++                    (o, g)
++                    for o, g in zip(outputs, grad_outputs)
++                    if g is not None and torch.is_tensor(o) and o.requires_grad
++                ]
++                if pairs:
++                    torch.autograd.backward(
++                        [o for o, _ in pairs], [g.to(o.dtype) for o, g in pairs]
++                    )
++        finally:
++            run_deferred_restores()
++        grads = [
++            x.grad if is_float else None for x, is_float in zip(inputs, ctx.float_inputs)
++        ]
++        return (None, None, *grads)

++def visible_forward(visible: Callable[..., Any], native: Callable[..., Any], *inputs: Any):
++    """``visible(*inputs)`` as the value, ``native(*inputs)``'s VJP as the gradient (see module docstring)."""
++    device = next(x.device for x in inputs if torch.is_tensor(x))
++    return VisibleNativeFunction.apply((visible, native), _anchor(device), *inputs)

++@contextlib.contextmanager
++def deployed_values(
++    params: Iterable[torch.nn.Parameter],
++    value_fn: Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor],
++    *,
++    active: bool = True,
++) -> Iterator[None]:
++    """Swap each master's data for ``value_fn(master)`` until :func:`run_deferred_restores`.
++
++    ``active=False`` is the identity (e.g. while the masters still sit exactly on the served
++    checkpoint grid). The masters may be views into a contiguous parameter buffer; the restore
++    puts the original storage back and checks it."""
++    if not active:
++        yield
++        return
++    params = list(params)
++    saved: list[torch.Tensor] = []
++    try:
++        for param in params:
++            saved.append(param.data)
++            param.data = value_fn(param.data)
++    except BaseException:
++        for param, data in zip(params, saved):
++            param.data = data
++        raise
++
++    def restore() -> None:
++        for param, data in zip(params, saved):
++            param.data = data
++            if param.data.data_ptr() != data.data_ptr():
++                raise RuntimeError("master restore did not re-point into the original storage")
++
++    _DEFERRED.append(restore)
++    yield
++

++@dataclass(frozen=True)
++class InProcessEngineConfig:
++    """Engine settings. Kernel-selecting fields (KV dtype, MoE backend, eager) must match the rollout's."""
++
++    gpu_memory_utilization: float = 0.15
++    # Fixed KV-cache size instead of what gpu_memory_utilization leaves after the
++    # profile run: the engine only ever holds one micro-batch.
++    kv_cache_memory_bytes: int | None = None
++    max_model_len: int = 8192
++    # Must cover the largest micro-batch: each micro-batch runs as one prefill step.
++    max_num_batched_tokens: int = 65536
++    # > 1: one vLLM DP=EP engine spread over the caller's torch.distributed world
++    # (world size == data_parallel_size), the layout of a DP=EP rollout.
++    data_parallel_size: int = 1
++    kv_cache_dtype: str = "fp8"
++    moe_backend: str | None = "triton"

++    # construction so other engines in this process are unaffected.
++    previous = os.environ.get("VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING")
++    os.environ["VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING"] = "0"
++    try:
++        yield
++    finally:
++        if previous is None:
++            os.environ.pop("VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING", None)
++        else:
++            os.environ["VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING"] = previous

++def build_inprocess_engine(model_path: str, config: InProcessEngineConfig, **llm_kwargs: Any):

++        max_model_len=config.max_model_len,
++        gpu_memory_utilization=config.gpu_memory_utilization,
++        enforce_eager=config.enforce_eager,
++        seed=config.seed,
++        enable_prefix_caching=False,
++        max_num_batched_tokens=config.max_num_batched_tokens,
++    )
++    if config.moe_backend is not None:

++    if config.tokenizer_mode is not None:

++            enable_expert_parallel=True,
++            distributed_executor_backend="external_launcher",
++        )
++    kwargs.update(llm_kwargs)
++    with _in_process_engine_core():
++        llm = LLM(**kwargs)

++    return llm, model

++class RoutingCapture:
++    """Expert ids selected by vLLM FusedMoE routers, captured through their routing-replay output.
++
++    vLLM's FusedMoE router copies each step's ``topk_ids`` into ``router._routing_replay_out`` when that buffer is
++    bound (the hook vLLM's own routed-experts capture binds). One buffer per layer; ``reset`` before a forward
++    fills them with -1 so a router that did not write, or wrote a different number of rows, is detected."""
++
++    def __init__(self, routers: dict[int, Any], *, max_tokens: int, top_k: int, device):
++        self._buffers: dict[int, torch.Tensor] = {}
++        for layer, router in routers.items():
++            if not hasattr(router, "_routing_replay_out"):
++                raise RuntimeError(f"layer {layer}: vLLM router has no routing-replay output")
++            if router._routing_replay_out is not None:
++                raise RuntimeError(f"layer {layer}: routing-replay output already bound")
++            buffer = torch.full((max_tokens, top_k), -1, dtype=torch.int16, device=device)
++            router._routing_replay_out = buffer
++            self._buffers[layer] = buffer
++
++    def reset(self) -> None:
++        for buffer in self._buffers.values():
++            buffer.fill_(-1)
++
++    def take(self, layer: int, num_tokens: int) -> torch.Tensor:
++        """The ids of the last forward's first ``num_tokens`` rows, as int64 ``[num_tokens, top_k]``."""
++        buffer = self._buffers[layer]
++        if num_tokens > buffer.shape[0]:
++            raise RuntimeError(f"layer {layer}: {num_tokens} tokens > capture capacity {buffer.shape[0]}")
++        ids = buffer[:num_tokens]
++        if bool((ids < 0).any()) or (
++            num_tokens < buffer.shape[0] and bool((buffer[num_tokens] >= 0).any())
++        ):
++            raise RuntimeError(
++                f"layer {layer}: the router did not route exactly {num_tokens} tokens in this forward"
++            )
++        return ids.to(torch.int64).clone()
++
++
++WeightLoader = Callable[[Any, Any, Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]], int]

++def _vllm_reload_weights(llm, model, weights: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> int:
++    del model
++    weights = list(weights)
++    llm.collective_rpc("reload_weights", kwargs={"weights_iterator": iter(weights)})
++    return len(weights)
++

++def resolve_weight_loader(spec: str) -> tuple[WeightLoader, Callable[[], None] | None]:
++    """``"vllm"``: vLLM's in-place ``reload_weights``. Otherwise the import path of a module exposing
++    ``load_weights(llm, model, weights) -> int`` and optionally ``prepare_engine()`` (called before the engine is
++    built). The engine must reload exactly as the rollout does, so integrations whose rollout uses its own loader
++    pass that loader here."""
++    if spec == "vllm":
++        return _vllm_reload_weights, None
++    module = importlib.import_module(spec)
++    return module.load_weights, getattr(module, "prepare_engine", None)
++

++def sparse_prefill_request(
++    q: torch.Tensor,
++    workspace: torch.Tensor,
++    topk_indices: torch.Tensor,
++    *,
++    seq_len: int,
++    query_len: int,
++    window_size: int,

++    """One request's sparse prefill exactly as ``_forward_prefill`` lowers it.
++
++    ``workspace`` is ``[N + seq_len, D]``: the request's compressed rows at
++    ``[0, N)`` and its SWA rows (all ``seq_len`` tokens) at ``[N, N + seq_len)``.
++    ``q`` holds the last ``query_len`` tokens of the request.  The attention list
++    of each token is built by vLLM's own ``combine_topk_swa_indices`` (top-k part
++    then the chronological window), so list order -- the order the ragged kernel
++    accumulates in -- is the rollout's.

++    from vllm.models.deepseek_v4.amd.rocm import combine_topk_swa_indices
++    from vllm.v1.attention.ops.rocm_aiter_mla_sparse import rocm_sparse_attn_prefill

++def indexer_topk_request(
++    q_fp8: torch.Tensor,
++    weights: torch.Tensor,
++    k_fp8: torch.Tensor,
++    k_scale: torch.Tensor,
++    positions: torch.Tensor,
++    *,
++    ratio: int,
++    out: torch.Tensor,
++) -> None:
++    """One request's C4 indexer top-k as ``rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer`` prefills.
++
++    Logits of the request's queries against its own compressed K (FP8 rows and
++    FP32 scales exactly as the cache holds them), then the batch-invariant
++    deterministic top-k: row-local ascending indices, -1 padded, into ``out``.
++    """
++    from vllm.v1.attention.ops.rocm_aiter_mla_sparse import (
++        dsv4_det_topk_per_row,
++        rocm_fp8_mqa_logits,
++    )

++    rows = q_fp8.shape[0]
++    row_starts = torch.zeros(rows, dtype=torch.int32, device=q_fp8.device)
++    row_ends = (
++        torch.div(positions + 1, ratio, rounding_mode="floor")
++        .clamp_max(k_fp8.shape[0])
++        .to(torch.int32)
++    )
++    logits = rocm_fp8_mqa_logits(
++        q_fp8, (k_fp8, k_scale), weights, row_starts, row_ends
++    )
++    dsv4_det_topk_per_row(

++class _DeterministicRowGather(torch.autograd.Function):
++    """``source.index_select(0, index)`` with a run-to-run deterministic VJP.
++
++    ``index_select``'s backward is ``index_add_``, whose CUDA/HIP kernel adds
++    repeated rows with atomics (nondeterministic order unless the global
++    deterministic mode is on).  ``index_put_(accumulate=True)`` sorts the
++    indices and sums each row's contributions sequentially, in index order:
++    the same FP32 sums, in a fixed order, independent of any global flag.
++    """
++
++    @staticmethod
++    def forward(ctx, source: torch.Tensor, index: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
++        ctx.save_for_backward(index)
++        ctx.source_rows = source.shape[0]
++        return source.index_select(0, index)
++
++    @staticmethod
++    def backward(ctx, grad_output: torch.Tensor):
++        (index,) = ctx.saved_tensors
++        grad_source = grad_output.new_zeros(
++            (ctx.source_rows, *grad_output.shape[1:])
++        )
++        grad_source.index_put_((index,), grad_output, accumulate=True)
++        return grad_source, None
++
++
++def deterministic_row_gather(source: torch.Tensor, index: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
++    """Rows ``source[index]`` (same values as ``index_select``); deterministic backward."""
++    if not (torch.is_grad_enabled() and source.requires_grad):
++        return source.index_select(0, index)
++    return _DeterministicRowGather.apply(source, index)
++

++def sparse_attention_reference(
++    q: torch.Tensor,
++    workspace: torch.Tensor,
++    combined: torch.Tensor,
++    combined_lens: torch.Tensor,
++    sink: torch.Tensor,
++    scale: float,
++    *,
++    chunk_rows: int = 512,
++) -> torch.Tensor:
++    """Differentiable FP32 gather attention over the same lists (the VJP graph)."""
++    width = combined.shape[-1]
++    columns = torch.arange(width, device=combined.device)
++    outputs = []
++    for start in range(0, q.shape[0], chunk_rows):
++        stop = min(start + chunk_rows, q.shape[0])
++        idx = combined[start:stop].long()
++        valid = (columns.unsqueeze(0) < combined_lens[start:stop].unsqueeze(1)) & (
++            idx >= 0
++        )
++        safe = torch.where(valid, idx, torch.zeros_like(idx))
++        kv = deterministic_row_gather(workspace.float(), safe.reshape(-1)).view(
++            stop - start, width, -1
++        )
++        scores = torch.einsum("thd,tkd->thk", q[start:stop].float(), kv) * scale
++        scores = scores.masked_fill(~valid.unsqueeze(1), float("-inf"))
++        logits = torch.cat(
++            (
++                scores,
++                sink.float().view(1, -1, 1).expand(scores.shape[0], -1, 1),
++            ),
++            dim=-1,
++        )
++        probs = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)[..., :-1]
++        outputs.append(torch.einsum("thk,tkd->thd", probs, kv).to(q.dtype))
++    return torch.cat(outputs, dim=0)
++

++def rollout_ep_combine(
++    route_values: torch.Tensor,
++    topk_ids: torch.Tensor,
++    *,
++    num_experts: int,
++    rollout_ep: int,
++) -> torch.Tensor:
++    """Reproduce the rollout's routed sum for its EP layout, bitwise.
++
++    Rank ``r`` of a rollout EP group of size ``E`` owns experts
++    ``[r * n / E, (r + 1) * n / E)`` (linear placement).  Its ``moe_sum`` adds
++    all ``K`` slots of a token in slot order in FP32 starting from 0 -- slots
++    of other ranks hold exact zeros -- and rounds to BF16; the batch-invariant
++    reduce-scatter then adds the ``E`` partials in rank order in FP32 starting
++    from rank 0's and rounds once.  ``route_values`` is ``[T, K, H]`` BF16
++    (router weight applied), ``topk_ids`` ``[T, K]`` global expert ids.
++    """
++    if num_experts % rollout_ep:
++        raise ValueError("rollout EP must divide the routed experts")
++    owner = torch.div(topk_ids.long(), num_experts // rollout_ep, rounding_mode="floor")
++    zero = route_values.new_zeros((), dtype=torch.float32)
++    total = None
++    for rank in range(rollout_ep):
++        partial = torch.zeros(
++            route_values.shape[0],
++            route_values.shape[2],
++            dtype=torch.float32,
++            device=route_values.device,
++        )
++        for slot in range(route_values.shape[1]):
++            mine = (owner[:, slot] == rank).unsqueeze(-1)
++            partial = partial + torch.where(mine, route_values[:, slot].float(), zero)
++        partial = partial.to(route_values.dtype).float()
++        total = partial if total is None else total + partial
++    return total.to(route_values.dtype)
++
++
++def owner_ranks(topk_ids: torch.Tensor, num_experts: int, ep: int) -> torch.Tensor:
++    return torch.div(topk_ids, num_experts // ep, rounding_mode="floor")

++# --- Segment-sum VJP of the row gather -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
++# Bitwise-exact, faster VJP for the row gather. The current VJP, zeros(rows).index_put_((index,), g, accumulate=True),
++# stable-sorts the indices and, per destination row, adds that row's contributions SERIALLY in sorted (= original)
++# order in FP32, starting from +0. Its cost is the hot row: every masked top-k/SWA slot is redirected to row 0
++# (``safe = where(valid, idx, 0)``) with an all-zero gradient row, so row 0 gets up to hundreds of thousands of
++# dependent adds per call (on the CP rank holding the first quarter of a sequence, most top-k slots are masked).
++# This VJP computes the same per-row sequential FP32 sums in the same order, but
++#   1. drops contributions whose gradient row is entirely +-0 (exact: the accumulator starts at +0 and can never become
++#      -0, and x + (+-0) == x bitwise for every x != -0, NaN included);
++#   2. stable-sorts the remaining indices (same relative order as index_put_'s stable sort);
++#   3. one Triton program per (destination row, column block) sums that row's segment sequentially from +0.
++# => bitwise identical to index_put_(accumulate=True) for FP32 (gate: torch.equal), deterministic run-to-run.
++# MLITE_DSV4_GATHER_BWD=index_put restores the original backward. Non-FP32 gradients always use index_put_.
++import os as _os
++
++
++@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1)
++def _segsum_kernels():
++    import triton
++    import triton.language as tl
++
++    @triton.jit
++    def _row_segment_sum(grad_ptr, perm_ptr, bounds_ptr, out_ptr, D, stride_g, BD: tl.constexpr):
++        r = tl.program_id(0)
++        cols = tl.program_id(1) * BD + tl.arange(0, BD)
++        m = cols < D
++        s = tl.load(bounds_ptr + r)
++        e = tl.load(bounds_ptr + r + 1)
++        acc = tl.zeros([BD], dtype=tl.float32)
++        for j in range(s, e):
++            src = tl.load(perm_ptr + j)
++            acc += tl.load(grad_ptr + src * stride_g + cols, mask=m, other=0.0)
++        tl.store(out_ptr + r.to(tl.int64) * D + cols, acc, mask=m)
++
++    return triton, _row_segment_sum
++
++
++def segmented_row_scatter_add(grad_output: torch.Tensor, index: torch.Tensor, rows: int) -> torch.Tensor:
++    """Bitwise ``zeros(rows, ...).index_put_((index,), grad_output, accumulate=True)`` for FP32 ``grad_output``."""
++    tail = grad_output.shape[1:]
++    n = index.numel()
++    g = grad_output.reshape(n, -1)
++    if g.stride(-1) != 1:
++        g = g.contiguous()
++    d = g.shape[1]
++    out = torch.empty((rows, d), dtype=torch.float32, device=g.device)
++    if n == 0 or d == 0:
++        return out.zero_().view(rows, *tail)
++    idx = index.reshape(-1).long()
++    keep = torch.nonzero((g != 0).any(dim=1)).squeeze(1)       # original order
++    sorted_idx, p = torch.sort(idx.index_select(0, keep), stable=True)
++    perm = keep.index_select(0, p)
++    bounds = torch.searchsorted(sorted_idx, torch.arange(rows + 1, device=idx.device, dtype=sorted_idx.dtype))
++    triton, row_segment_sum = _segsum_kernels()
++    bd = 128 if d >= 128 else triton.next_power_of_2(d)
++    row_segment_sum[(rows, triton.cdiv(d, bd))](g, perm, bounds, out, d, g.stride(0), BD=bd, num_warps=2)
++    return out.view(rows, *tail)

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# GRPO/DAPO | DeepSeek-V4-Flash FP8 | true on-policy | vLLM rollout + Megatron | AMD ROCm (MI355X, gfx950)
+#
+# One recipe and one image; VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT alone selects the arm:
+#   VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 (default)  consistent arm: batch-invariant vLLM rollout, Megatron mLite actor with the
+#                                     vLLM-aligned implementation (actor_rollout_ref.actor.engine.impl=ALIGNED_ACTOR_IMPL),
+#                                     rollout log-probs == trainer log-probs bitwise.
+#   VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0            native baseline: default vLLM kernels, Megatron-Core actor (model_engine=megatron)
+#                                     with FP8 QAT and routing replay (R3), as the merged ROCm recipe
+#                                     run_deepseek_v4_flash_megatron_rocm.sh trains it.
+# Algorithm, data, lengths, batch, optimizer hyper-parameters and rollout layout are shared by both arms.
+# Modelled on verl-project/verl#7688 (examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_true_on_policy_preview_megatron.sh).
+#
+# Image: docker/rocm/Dockerfile.rocm.deepseek-v4.true-on-policy (vLLM 0.26.0 + batch-invariance patches, Megatron-LM
+# with mLite impl=vllm on ROCm). The full-profile defaults are the configuration of the validated 4-node run:
+# rollout_probs_diff_max 0.0 on every step, including steps after exact resumes.
+#
+# Container requirement: raise the open-file limit (docker run --ulimit nofile=1048576:1048576). With the default
+# limit, the multi-node full profile failed after ~26 steps in gloo ("Too many open files", tcp/device.cc).
+#
+# PROFILE
+#   proxy  1 node x 4 GPUs, MODEL_PATH = a 4-layer cut of the checkpoint, short lengths, 3 steps: the daily cell.
+#          A 4-layer cut never finishes an answer, so DAPO rewards are constant and every advantage is 0; pass a
+#          varying reward for real updates, e.g. reward.custom_reward_function.path=<file> ...name=compute_score.
+#   full   4 nodes x 8 GPUs, full checkpoint, the formal workload. Two-step acceptance = PROFILE=full
+#          TOTAL_TRAINING_STEPS=2 with nothing else changed (constant LR, no warmup, so the first two steps of the
+#          schedule are the formal ones).
+#
+# Required env: MODEL_PATH (HF directory with config.json and the tokenizer/chat template), TRAIN_FILES, VAL_FILES.
+# Multi-node: an existing Ray cluster (RAY_ADDRESS) whose workers run this image.
+# Modes: DRY_RUN=1 prints the arm environment and the full command; COMPOSE_ONLY=1 prints the resolved Hydra config.
+# Extra arguments are passed to verl.trainer.main_ppo as Hydra overrides (last wins).
+set -euo pipefail
+
+die() {
+  printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2
+  exit 64
+}
+
+# --- Arm --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+export VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT="${VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT:-1}"
+case "${VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT}" in
+  0|1) ;;
+  *) die "VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT must be 0 or 1, got '${VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT}'" ;;

+PROFILE="${PROFILE:-full}"
+SEED="${SEED:-42}"
+# mLite engine implementation of the consistent arm (actor_rollout_ref.actor.engine.impl): `vllm` = the vLLM-aligned
+# DeepSeek-V4 forward on the rollout's own ROCm kernels with deterministic VJPs (the validated default);
+# `vllm_engine` = forward from an in-process vLLM engine (needs CP 1 and rollout DP = EP = actor EP).
+ALIGNED_ACTOR_IMPL="${ALIGNED_ACTOR_IMPL:-vllm}"
+HYDRA_OVERRIDES=("$@")
+
+: "${MODEL_PATH:?set MODEL_PATH to the DeepSeek-V4-Flash checkpoint (or its 4-layer cut for PROFILE=proxy)}"
+: "${TRAIN_FILES:?set TRAIN_FILES to the DAPO-format training parquet}"
+: "${VAL_FILES:?set VAL_FILES to the DAPO-format validation parquet}"
+[[ -s "${MODEL_PATH}/config.json" ]] || die "missing ${MODEL_PATH}/config.json"

+# --- Workload profile (shared by both arms) ---------------------------------------------------------------------

+  proxy)

+    : "${TRAIN_BATCH_SIZE:=4}" "${PPO_MINI_BATCH_SIZE:=4}" "${ROLLOUT_N:=4}"
+    : "${MAX_PROMPT_LENGTH:=2048}" "${MAX_RESPONSE_LENGTH:=2048}" "${OVERLONG_BUFFER_LEN:=512}"
